newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end at fourth straight record.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end at fourth straight record.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed up at their fourth straight record, but erratic trade and profit-taking towards the end of the session could herald declines later this week, traders said.
"The bolsa's been rising for a number of days now and in a healthy market one would expect some profit-taking to set in, perhaps tomorrow," Banesco broker Simon Brad said.

The bolsa's 19-share index ended ahead 0.51 percent at 9,515.75 points paring earlier gains that saw it touch 9,738 points. A total of 108 million shares traded, worth 12 billion bolivars ($24.5 million), according to preliminary figures.
"The bolsa opened strong, up more than two percent, but closed down on profit-taking ... hard to say if by foreign funds or local investors," added Brad.

Among traded stocks, 25 rose, 14 fell and seven closed flat, as leading utility Electricidad de Caracas continued its month-long rally, closing up 11.25 bolivars at 825.25. The company was awarded a 75 percent tariff increase June 26.
Merinvest's composite index, which includes telephone company CANTV, meanwhile closed up 0.42 percent at 148.93 points.
